pr_body:
Fixes #16028

This adds the internal `int conn_gets(BIO *bio, char *buf, int size)` to `bss_conn.c` 
for use with HTTP connections to servers returning text (rather than ASN.1 structures).
Its code is similar to `BIO_get_line()` recently added in #12959.

##### Checklist
<!-- Remove items that do not apply. For completed items, change [ ] to [x]. -->
- [x] documentation is added or updated
- [x] tests are added or updated
pr_comments:
Thanks for the immediate approval.

> Unsure if this should be in 3.0

I'd say yes because it fixes a bug in the new HTTP client API:
otherwise `OSSL_HTTP_get()` etc. fail on getting non-ASN.1 contents.
The fix adds a capability to `BIO_s_connect()`, yet just internally, without changing the API.
This is a feature addition. Clearly the base code wasn't meant to work on non-ASN1 or it would have been tested and documented as doing that.

> This is a feature addition. Clearly the base code wasn't meant to work on non-ASN1 or it would have been tested and documented as doing that.

I would have fully agreed to this before the new HTTP client API was included.
Since then, it's also a bug fix for the new API.

As mentioned before, `OSSL_HTTP_get()` and the like do not work for non-ASN.1 contents such as HTML.
This is how I noticed that #16028 is meanwhile more than a non-feature: it has become a bug.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.

When the code base explicitly documents that BIO_gets() is not supported on a connect BIO and you are changing the code to add BIO_gets() support then you are by definition adding a feature. There is no wriggle room there.

> When the code base explicitly documents that `BIO_gets()` is not supported on a connect BIO and you are changing the code to add `BIO_gets()` support then you are by definition adding a feature. There is no wriggle room there.

Yes, and I agreed to that - see above.
My point here is a different one - again: meanwhile the missing feature turned into bug,
because the missing feature causes the new HTTP client API not to work as expected and documented.

Me insisting that it's (meanwhile also) a bug does not imply that I insist in getting the fix into 3.0 - 
to me the issue is not urgent, but I would vote in favor of fixing the bug immediately (i..e, for 3.0):
If it is not included, it's likely there will be 3.0 users hitting this bug and (rightfully) complain about it.
So I don't think it would be good strategy to delay the bug fix for some (questionable, in this case) formal reasons.

The OTC should decide whether to have this bug fixed in 3.0 or thereafter.

The bug might also be fixable in a different way, without extending the semantics of `BIO_s_connect()`.
Suggestions and implementations are welcome. Yet they only make sense if they lead to a fix that is included with 3.0.

IMO this should not go into 3.0. We are not obligated to fix all the bugs (or things that someone claims is a bug) in the existing releases.
This can be merged to master branch.

> IMO this should not go into 3.0. We are not obligated to fix all the bugs (or things that someone claims is a bug) in the existing releases.

Yet how do you propose then to handle the issue I mentioned in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/16028#issuecomment-876653878:

_It turns out that the missing BIO gets support causes a bug in the new HTTP client API:
attempting to get a response in non-ASN.1 form (e.g., plain HTML text) leads to the error reported above._


> This can be merged to master branch.

Can this be done right away?

> Yet how do you propose then to handle the issue I mentioned in [#16028 (comment)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/16028#issuecomment-876653878):

Not to fix it? Perhaps document it as known issue?
This pull request is ready to merge

Merged to master. Thank you @DDvO 

As for whether there is anything acceptable for 3.0 I do not know. But IMO this one isn't. Definitely not without explicit OTC exception.

> > Yet how do you propose then to handle the issue I mentioned in [#16028 (comment)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/16028#issuecomment-876653878):
>>> It turns out that the missing BIO gets support causes a bug in the new HTTP client API:
>>> attempting to get a response in non-ASN.1 form (e.g., plain HTML text) leads to the error reported above.
> 
> Not to fix it? Perhaps document it as known issue?

Meanwhile I found and applied a viable workaround for 3.0, see #17066.

issue_context.title: Connect BIOs support `BIO_read()` and `BIO_puts()` but fail to support `BIO_gets()`
issue_context.body:
Adapting a library that uses the legacy HTTP client API to OpenSSL 3.0,
I ran into the interesting problem that `BIO_s_connect()` returns a BIO method that does not support `BIO_gets()` and got
```
...:error:10000079:BIO routines:BIO_gets:unsupported method:crypto/bio/bio_lib.c:459:
```

In `bss_conn.c` I found
```
static const BIO_METHOD methods_connectp = {
    BIO_TYPE_CONNECT,
    "socket connect",
    bwrite_conv,
    conn_write,
    bread_conv,
    conn_read,
    conn_puts,
    NULL,                       /* conn_gets, */
    conn_ctrl,
    conn_new,
    conn_free,
    conn_callback_ctrl,
};
```
and the documentation says
```
       Read and write operations on a connect BIO will perform I/O on the underlying connection. If no connection is
       established and the port and hostname (see below) is set up properly then a connection is established first.

       Connect BIOs support BIO_puts() but not BIO_gets().
```
so apparently this is considered a (non-)feature, not a bug - why?
comments:
It turns out that the missing BIO gets support causes a bug in the new HTTP client API:
attempting to get a response in non-ASN.1 form (e.g., plain HTML text) leads to the error reported above.

SSL BIOs also do not support `gets`, but it looks like there is no efficient and simple solution for this.

Yet there are two workarounds, as documented in `BIO_read.pod`:

       If the "gets" method is not supported by a BIO then BIO_get_line() can be used.
       It is also possible to make BIO_gets() usable even if the "gets" method is not
       supported by adding a buffering BIO BIO_f_buffer(3) to the chain.

review_comments:
I deliberately left them apart (as done also for `BIO_get_line()`)
because as soon as input validation of `buf` and `size` is successful, ` *buf = '\0';` can be done,
which is defensive in case an error is returned due to `bio == NULL || bio->ptr == NULL` but ignored by the caller.

when I compile this with gcc-4.8.x I get a warning here:
```
test/http_test.c: In function 'test_http_keep_alive':
test/http_test.c:211:5: error: initializer element is not computable at load time [-Werror]
     server_args mock_args = { NULL, content_type, NULL, '0', 0 };
     ^
cc1: all warnings being treated as errors
```

gcc-4.8.x appears rather old.
The code section you highlighted above was a bit confusing, but given the compiler warning message I found what the issue is. Fix is in #17308.
